verdict: UNDECIDABLE ON PUBLIC DATA (requires multi-sector continuous PLATO/TESS or long-baseline high-precision RV monitoring to separate from quarterly roll systematics)
verdict_reasoning: In Kepler long-cadence public archival data across Quarters 0-17, the 65.157-day signal reported in the McQuillan (2014) catalog exhibits low spectral significance in standard stitched PDCSAP and is heavily masked by long-term instrumental drift in unconditioned SAP flux. Because 65.2 days represents ~70% of a Kepler quarter (~93.125 days) and lies between the 5th (74.50d) and 6th (62.08d) harmonics of the Kepler orbital period (372.5d), instrumental quarter-roll discontinuities and thermal drift prevent definitive distinction between genuine stellar rotation and systematic artifacts on public Kepler pipeline data alone. Decisive confirmation or refutation requires multi-year ground-based radial velocity or continuous multi-sector high-precision photometry (such as extended multi-year TESS or PLATO long-duration monitoring) free of 90-day roll discontinuities.
